brief.headline: Samsung/Hynix bounce 6.8%/4.6% after Thursday's Meta-driven rout; $518B capex plan unveiled, HBM sold out through 2026
brief.summary: <cite index="37-2,37-6">Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix stocks rebounded on Friday as bargain hunters returned after Thursday's bruising sell-off.</cite> <cite index="38-10">Samsung fell 9.06% and SK Hynix dropped 14.57% on Thursday</cite>, triggered by fears Meta's surplus AI capacity signals infrastructure peak. <cite index="42-4">Samsung and SK Hynix jointly committed 800 trillion won ($518 billion) to build four new memory fabs and an HBM packaging hub</cite>, with government fast-tracking timelines. <cite index="4-4,4-20">HBM capacity is fully allocated for 2026, with Micron guiding 68% gross margin in Q2 2026.</cite> <cite index="10-6,10-7">DRAM contract prices continue to rise driven by tight supply and expectations of negative production growth.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: Long SK Hynix vs. short Samsung. <cite index="5-3">Hynix controlled 57% of global HBM revenue share in Q4 2025, versus Samsung at 22%.</cite> <cite index="4-15,4-16">SK Hynix has emerged as the primary HBM beneficiary and is the only supplier able to deliver both HBM3E and HBM4 at scale.</cite> <cite index="9-8">Hynix expects HBM4 pricing roughly 40% higher than HBM3E, even after absorbing a 50% rise in cost per bit.</cite> Samsung's catch-up capex dilutes near-term ROI while Hynix defends customer lock-in (Nvidia, Blackwell/Rubin) at premium pricing. Risk: Samsung closes HBM qualification gap faster than expected, eroding Hynix's margin umbrella.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="12-2,12-7">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, while NAND Flash jumped 70-75% QoQ.</cite> <cite index="11-10">Q1 2026 saw DRAM prices rise 93-98% QoQ—buyers paid roughly double versus three months earlier.</cite> <cite index="4-1">Manufacturers are diverting production lines toward HBM stacks and enterprise-grade DDR5, squeezing supply of flash and mobile memory.</cite> <cite index="13-22">Hyperscaler capex projected to exceed $600 billion in 2026, up 40% YoY.</cite> Relief not expected until late 2027/2028 when new fab capacity (Micron Singapore, SK Cheongju, Samsung Pyeongtaek) comes online.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="4-19,4-20">Top three memory makers have already allocated full HBM output for the year, with Micron guiding 68% gross margin in Q2 2026.</cite> <cite index="9-3">SK Hynix will likely secure ~50% of total HBM bits in 2026.</cite> <cite index="9-7,9-8">Hynix expects minimal to modest HBM3E pricing downtick for 2026 versus 2025, but commands ~40% premium on HBM4 first-mover advantage.</cite> <cite index="3-4">HBM expected to remain in short supply until 2026 [note: article from mid-2025, constraint persisting].</cite> Nvidia Blackwell uses 8 HBM sites (vs. 5 in H100), intensifying bit demand. Samsung's delayed ramp injects competitive tension but supply remains allocated.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung/SK Hynix rebound 6.8%/4.6% after Thursday's 9%/14.5% selloff on Meta capacity fears
news_pulse.implication: Bargain buying after overreaction. Mirae Asset: global big-tech capex $806B in 2026, up 73% YoY. Meta surplus narrative overstated versus HBM tightness reality.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung & SK Hynix commit $518B for four new memory fabs, HBM packaging hub
news_pulse.implication: Government fast-tracking construction approvals; SK Hynix Yongin 4th fab moved from 2045 to 2033. New capacity arrives 2028+, leaving current cycle undersupplied.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix announces 100 trillion won ($64B) domestic investment, M17 NAND fab targeted H1 2029
news_pulse.implication: 80T won to M17 NAND, 20T won to P&T7 advanced packaging. Addresses enterprise SSD shortage (NAND now rising faster than DRAM for first time this cycle).

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity doubled to 130K wafers/month by end-2026; Nvidia secured >60% allocation
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS-L/S fully booked. TSMC outsourcing 240-270K wafers annually to Amkor/SPIL. Packaging remains AI accelerator chokepoint through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex guidance: $690-900B, up 36-81% YoY; Amazon alone $200B
news_pulse.implication: Sequoia's Cahn: $600B annual revenue gap between hyperscaler AI spend and ecosystem sales, widening in 2026. Memory suppliers pre-allocate to hyperscalers.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM prices quadrupled over past year; Q1 2026 up 93-98% QoQ (record), Q2 +58-63% QoQ
news_pulse.implication: HBM consumes 3x wafer area of DDR5. Industry revenue $97B in Q1 2026, up 81% QoQ. Spot market buyers no longer chasing higher quotes—parabolic phase maturing.

news_pulse.headline: NAND prices surged 70-75% QoQ in Q2 2026, outpacing DRAM for first time this cycle
news_pulse.implication: Enterprise SSD demand absorbing capacity. eMMC/UFS segment faces tightest supply gap. Client SSD buyers restocking preemptively out of allocation fear.

news_pulse.headline: Micron, SK Hynix hit $1T market cap; memory stocks up 114-186% YTD through May 2026
news_pulse.implication: SK Hynix up 1,000% over 12 months. Counterpoint: HBM demand expected to exceed supply over next 3 years. Risk: structural supply shortage thesis vs. cyclicality debate.

brief.derivatives_signal: KOSPI 200 futures likely saw heavy put-selling Friday as index recovered +3% from Thursday's -7.89% plunge. ADR premia (SSNLF/HXSCL) compressed after Thursday dislocation. Watch for gamma exposure flip if Samsung breaks 305K won resistance (Friday close). Volatility surface pricing in elevated tail risk post-Meta headlines, but realized vol subsiding. Option skew favors upside on Hynix (HBM lock-in), downside protection on Samsung (execution risk).
watch_for_next_3h: KOSPI follow-through above 7,900 or fade below 7,800—tests whether Friday's bounce was short-covering or conviction buying
Any hyperscaler (MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL) commentary on Q2 capex execution or Blackwell/MI350 deployment timelines
